title: The structure-sheaf sequence of a projective hypersurface
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$ and $d\geq1$ integers, $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ with each variable of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $F\in S$ a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)=\mathbf P^n_k$ and $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(S/(F))$ [def-pc-proj], with its quotient closed subscheme structure and canonical closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The sequence of $\mathcal O_P$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_P(-d)\xrightarrow{\,F\,}\mathcal O_P\xrightarrow{\,r\,}i_*\mathcal O_Z\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact, where $\mathcal O_P(-d)$ is the standard twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], and $r$ is the actual structure-sheaf restriction map. Under $\mathcal O_P(-d)=\widetilde{S(-d)}$, $\mathcal O_P=\widetilde S$, and $i_*\mathcal O_Z=\widetilde{S/(F)}$, the displayed arrows are the sheafifications of multiplication by $F$ and the quotient map. On $D_+(x_j)$ the first arrow sends the twist generator $x_j^{-d}$ to $F/x_j^d$. On every positive homogeneous basic open $D_+(g)$, the final identification is with $((S/(F))_g)_0$ and the restriction arrow sends $a/g^m$ to $\bar a/\bar g^m$. These identifications respect restrictions. The ideal is $(F)$, without replacing it by its radical; no reducedness, irreducibility, smoothness, or characteristic assumption is made.

proof.text: Write $C=S/(F)$ with its quotient grading and let $q:S\to C$ be the quotient map. The graded map $u:S(-d)\to S$ sends $a$ to $Fa$: an element of degree $r$ in $S(-d)$ lies in $S_{r-d}$, hence its image lies in $S_r$. The quotient map preserves degrees. Multiplication by $F$ is injective: order monomials lexicographically on the finite ordered variables; for any nonzero $a$, the largest monomial of $Fa$ is the product of the largest monomials of $F$ and $a$, with coefficient the product of their nonzero coefficients in $k$, hence is nonzero. By the definition of the principal ideal, $\ker q=(F)=\operatorname{im}u$, and every class in $C$ has a representative in $S$. Thus $0\to S(-d)\xrightarrow{u}S\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ is an exact sequence of graded $S$-modules. The ideal $(F)$ is homogeneous since multiplying each homogeneous component of a polynomial by $F$ shifts its degree by $d$.

source.place: Tag 0BYD, lemma-genus-plane-curve, first displayed graded exact sequence; elementary verification in n+1 variables

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proj-graded-sheafification-exact] to the graded exact sequence of Step 1 over the nonnegatively graded ring $S$. It gives the short exact sequence $0\to\widetilde{S(-d)}\xrightarrow{\widetilde u}\widetilde S\xrightarrow{\widetilde q}\widetilde C\to0$ of $\mathcal O_P$-modules. By [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial], on every positive homogeneous chart $D_+(g)$ these maps are $a/g^m\mapsto Fa/g^m$ and $b/g^m\mapsto\bar b/\bar g^m$, respectively, where for the second formula the target is first viewed as the degree-zero localization of the graded $S$-module $C$. The shift in Step 1 makes the first formula degree-preserving. Both cited statements apply to arbitrary $S$ and arbitrary integer-graded modules, not just to the projective line.

source.place: Tag 01M7, lemma-proj-sheaves, functoriality and final exactness assertion

proof.text: The definitions give $\widetilde{S(-d)}=\mathcal O_P(-d)$ and $\widetilde S=\mathcal O_P$. Fix $j$ and put $U_j=D_+(x_j)$. For every positive-degree homogeneous $g$ with $D_+(g)\subseteq U_j$, $x_j$ is a unit of $S_g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion](1); hence $a\mapsto a\,x_j^{-d}$ and $b\mapsto b\,x_j^{d}$ are mutually inverse $S_{(g)}$-linear maps between $S_{(g)}=\mathcal O_P(D_+(g))$ and $(S_g)_{-d}=\widetilde{S(-d)}(D_+(g))$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf](2). Both maps commute with the restrictions, which are localization maps, and $x_j^{-d}$ restricts to $x_j^{-d}$. Standard opens inside $U_j$ form a basis of $U_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion](0), so [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](a),(b) make $a\mapsto a\,x_j^{-d}$ an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{U_j}\cong\widetilde{S(-d)}|_{U_j}$ of $\mathcal O_{U_j}$-modules: $x_j^{-d}$ is a frame. On $U_j\cap U_l$, $x_j^{-d}=(x_j/x_l)^{-d}x_l^{-d}$, which is exactly the transition rule $e_j^{(-d)}=(x_j/x_l)^{-d}e_l^{(-d)}$ of the standard twist of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. The coordinate opens cover $P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-polynomial-twist-chart], so the isomorphisms $e_j^{(-d)}\mapsto x_j^{-d}$ agree on overlaps and glue to an isomorphism from the specified twist onto the shifted-module sheaf. The formula of Step 2 sends the frame $x_j^{-d}=1/x_j^d$ (numerator $1\in S(-d)_d$) to $F/x_j^d$.

source.place: Tag 01MN, definition-twist; Tag 01MS, lemma-when-invertible, frame on a degree-one chart

proof.text: Apply the chart clause of [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] to the surjective graded map $S\to C$. Its hypotheses hold because $S$ is generated by its variables in degree one. Thus $i^{-1}D_+(g)=D_+(\bar g)$ for every positive-degree homogeneous $g$, and the actual scheme morphism on these charts is given by $S_{(g)}\to C_{(\bar g)}$, $a/g^m\mapsto\bar a/\bar g^m$. By [def-pc-proj], $\Gamma(D_+(\bar g),\mathcal O_Z)=C_{(\bar g)}$. The localization of $C$ as an $S$-module at $g$ is the localization of the ring $C$ at $\bar g$: both have representatives $c/g^m$ and the relation $g^t(g^rc-g^mc')=0$ in $C$. Their degree-zero parts coincide. Hence these formulas give $\mathcal O_P(D_+(g))$-linear identifications $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)(D_+(g))=(C_g)_0=\widetilde C(D_+(g))$, the last equality by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists](b).

The identifications of Step 4 commute with restrictions. Explicitly, for $D_+(h)\subseteq D_+(g)$ choose $h^e=bg$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists](a). On $\widetilde C$, restriction sends $c/g^m$ to $b^mc/h^{em}$. On $Z$, $\bar h^e=\bar b\bar g$, so the structure-sheaf restriction sends the same class to $\bar b^mc/\bar h^{em}$; these are the identical fraction in $C_{\bar h}$. The scalar maps are identical quotient-localization maps as well. Standard opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion](0); therefore [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](a),(b) glues these mutually inverse identifications into an $\mathcal O_P$-linear isomorphism $\widetilde C\cong i_*\mathcal O_Z$. On every basis open the composite of $\widetilde q$ with this isomorphism is $a/g^m\mapsto\bar a/\bar g^m$, which Step 4 identifies with the actual structure-sheaf restriction. Equality on the basis gives equality of these sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 01M7 (1)--(3), fraction restriction maps; Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj (2)

proof.text: Substitute the identifications of Steps 3 and 5 into the short exact sequence of Step 2. Its two arrows become multiplication by $F$ and the actual map $r$, with exactly the chart and restriction formulas already computed. The construction throughout uses the quotient ring $S/(F)$ itself. For example if $F=x_0^d$ with $d>1$, its nilpotents remain in the quotient charts; when $\bar g$ is nilpotent the localized ring is zero and the corresponding open of $Z$ is empty, so the same formulas still hold. No step replaces $(F)$ by its radical or requires smoothness, irreducibility, reducedness, or any condition on the characteristic.
